summary: Dispatch, run-status, committed-slice integration, coordination preflight, and runtime-blocker-taxonomy tools.

tools.notes: MCP-only agent role dispatch for worker, reviewer, and redteam. The normal call supplies only role and subject. On every dispatch the launcher reads the role model from repo-root agent-launch.toml and derives app/backend through the neutral model registry; typed app/model are explicit per-dispatch overrides only. Missing, malformed, or unknown role configuration refuses actionably with no family fallback. Same-user stdio MCP is not an authentication boundary; the real boundary is the launcher sandbox plus work-record admission. Caller-supplied identity carriers (request payload, prompt text, ambient env, argv, claimed_identity.role) are refused and never become selection authority. Worker and reviewer accept a WK or slice; redteam also accepts an IN. Non-dispatchable subjects refuse with work_record_readiness_failure. Reviewer mutation authority is always empty. A canonical implementation slice already in review with a launcher-verified exact committed target is reviewed against that same subject without changing its declared delivery write_scope; other reviewer subjects with non-empty write_scope refuse with role_policy_violation / reviewer_write_scope_nonempty and require a separate findings-only review unit. Confined Claude and Codex sessions receive exactly one launcher-owned host wiki-MCP server through two private named FIFOs bound into the final bubblewrap namespace and the pinned copy-only relay; exact initialize and tools/list readiness is mandatory. Agy is unsupported and fails closed. Refusals use stable runtime-blocker taxonomy codes. Route worker/reviewer/redteam dispatch through this MCP tool only; if the launch backend is unconfigured, report the blocker rather than falling back to wrappers, shell, env, another transport, or bwrap changes.
use_when: The dispatch_role_call intent has a dispatchable workspace_validate_dispatch result for the same unit and role.
do_not_use_when: Readiness is unknown; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
The task asks about an existing run; use workspace_agent_run_status or workspace_agent_run_wait.
requires_prior_state: Same-unit same-role workspace_validate_dispatch result with dispatchable=true.

Missing, malformed, or unknown role configuration refuses actionably with no family fallback. A canonical implementation slice already in review with a launcher-verified exact committed target is reviewed against that same subject without changing its declared delivery write_scope; other reviewer subjects with non-empty write_scope refuse with role_policy_violation / reviewer_write_scope_nonempty and require a separate findings-only review unit. When CCE/Node Engine refusal output includes a valid worker_admission.recovery.v1 object, treat it as the primary recovery projection: pack_result.recovery is current-decision recovery, while top-level route-problem recovery applies before a pack_result exists. Both are advisory, non-authorizing, resubmission-only guidance; they do not satisfy review evidence, accepted authority, launcher policy, or admission. Legacy reason-fact recovery is compatibility-only when no valid recovery object is present. Malformed, unknown-version, unknown-field, or projection-mismatched recovery fails closed: preserve the underlying refusal, report bounded recovery-contract mismatch guidance, resubmit through CCE, and do not infer local admission, hidden controls, bypasses, or synthesized authorities. Route worker/reviewer/redteam dispatch through this MCP tool only; if the launch backend is unconfigured, report the blocker rather than falling back to wrappers, shell, env, another transport, or bwrap changes.

tools.notes: Monitor-handle status query for workspace_agent_dispatch. Refuses caller identity carriers and handle mismatch, replay, or unknown cases. NOT read-only for managed exact-slice worker runs: polling may prepare review state, integrate, update Git refs, and update canonical slice status. child_terminal reports only child exit; terminal:true means the COMPLETE managed run is finalized. Preserve scalar next_action. The bounded closeout_continuation is advisory only: it orders review, coordinator disposition for canonical changes_requested, integration, original-monitor resumption, terminal review, and handoff, and exposes at most the current safe call from retained canonical state. It grants no authority. Free/local structured_role_result.valid:false is expected under DEC-0128.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks for status, output, failure, or completion of an already dispatched run.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Bounded-wait companion to run-status: waits for a dispatched run to finish or until a bounded polling window expires, one response per call. The deadline covers both child completion and managed lifecycle finalization; a caller-action block returns promptly, while timed_out:true is a clean window expiry. Retry the same launcher-minted handle and never relaunch. NOT read-only for managed exact-slice worker runs: polling may prepare review state, integrate, update Git refs, and update canonical slice status. child_terminal reports only child exit; terminal:true means the COMPLETE managed run is finalized. It projects the same scalar next_action and bounded advisory closeout_continuation as run-status: canonical changes_requested requires coordinator disposition and suppresses integration or handoff as the current safe call. The continuation grants no authority. Free/local structured_role_result.valid:false is expected under DEC-0128.
use_when: The run_monitoring intent asks to wait briefly for an already dispatched run to finish.
do_not_use_when: The task is a new role launch; use workspace_validate_dispatch first.
No monitor handle is available; ask for it instead of searching, reading records, or relaunching.

tools.notes: Read-only schema-backed runtime blocker taxonomy: the canonical code catalog, categories, the deterministic degraded-state mapping, and the bootstrap-state subset. Dispatch (workspace_agent_dispatch) and the launcher must select blocker codes from this taxonomy rather than inventing ad hoc strings. reviewer_write_scope_nonempty is a structured reason on role_policy_violation (not a separate code); canonical committed implementation slices in review use launcher-owned exact-target admission with empty reviewer mutation authority, while other non-empty reviewer subjects require a separate findings-only review unit.

Read-only coordinator/orchestrator preflight: reports role, caller/session role, subject, allowed durable write surfaces (docs/, wiki/), the implementation/test edit prohibition, repo/docs/wiki writability, available structured dispatch/validation routes, and active runtime blocker codes. A fully read-only mount surfaces as read_only_mount (filesystem category), not as role policy. Caller-supplied identity carriers are refused; role and caller_session_role are caller-asserted introspection knobs.

Separate orchestrator continuation for exact committed-slice integration. Review evidence and comment dispositions are advisory; neither they nor the request authorize integration. CCE owns any configured policy gate. Paid-tier presence alone configures no gate; no configured gate follows DEC-0133 and reports non-audit posture. Input is closed to repo alias, canonical slice subject, and comment dispositions; authority carriers are rejected. The server re-derives the exact target and performs CAS-safe idempotent integration. Successful and idempotently recovered results advise resuming workspace_agent_run_status or workspace_agent_run_wait with the original launcher-minted handle; integration neither accepts nor returns that handle. Refusals omit the success continuation.
use_when: A committed implementation slice is parked after review preparation and the orchestrator is ready to disposition advisory comments and request integration.
do_not_use_when: The task is to dispatch or monitor a reviewer; use workspace_agent_dispatch or workspace_agent_run_status.
The caller intends to supply a ref, SHA, receipt, policy verdict, CCE attestation, or other authority carrier.
requires_prior_state: A canonical committed implementation slice in review with launcher-owned frozen target state.

tools.notes: Orchestrator/operator continuation for byte-identical publication of the exact terminal candidate. Reviewer results and monitor guidance are advisory: clean output cannot authorize and findings cannot veto. CCE alone decides a configured policy gate; no gate follows DEC-0133 and reports non-audit posture. Caller input is closed to workspace alias and WK assigned_unit; the server derives candidate, repository, remote, branch, and pull-request identity. Cold recovery reads only refs/agent-launch/terminal-current-v2/<WK> and accepts only an already-present, directly commit-valued, mechanically authenticated target; absence fails closed with terminal_candidate_recovery_current_ref_absent. Absent-ref construction remains confined to the hot post-worker lifecycle, where launcher-bound B/W/contracts exist and absence is the expected-old CAS state. Later landing movement does not invalidate unchanged C, and merge readiness remains with forge and policy. A retained canonically eligible clean terminal review may recommend this route, while changes_requested requires coordinator disposition. Candidate construction and handoff authority remain launcher-owned.
use_when: A terminal candidate is frozen and quiescent and the orchestrator is ready to request its exact forge publication.
do_not_use_when: The work record is still active, or an implementation slice or managed run is still open; finish the lifecycle first.
The task asks to merge, approve, rebase, or update an existing branch; the forge and organization policy own those.
authoritative_for: launcher-owned forge branch creation and pull-request create-or-observe
requires_prior_state: A launcher-frozen exact terminal candidate with canonical initiative assignment and a quiescent lifecycle.
Launcher-configured landing branch and a forge credential available host-side to the trusted server.
